title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction
During the first trimester of pregnancy, nutrition plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus. Prioritizing essential nutrients and safe foods will help ensure the health and well-being of both the mother and the baby.

## Folate and Iron
Folate and iron are two essential nutrients during the early stages of pregnancy. Folate helps prevent birth defects of the brain and spine, while iron supports the development of the fetus. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should take 400 micrograms of folic acid daily. Additionally, iron is also a crucial nutrient, and pregnant women should consume about 27 milligrams of iron per day.

## Safe Foods
During the first trimester, pregnant women should prioritize safe foods to avoid the risk of food poisoning. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi, sashimi, and undercooked or raw meat. Instead, they should opt for cooked foods, such as beef, chicken, and fish.

## Hydration
Water is an essential part of pregnancy nutrition. Pregnant women should drink enough water to support the development of the fetus and prevent digestive problems. According to the WHO, pregnant women should drink about 2 liters of water per day.

## Sample Meal Plan
Here are some sample meal ideas for pregnant women during the first trimester:
- Breakfast: Oatmeal with fruit and milk
- Lunch: Cooked chicken with rice and vegetables
- Dinner: Grilled fish with salad and fruit

## Important Notes
Pregnant women should consult their doctor before making any changes to their diet. Additionally, they should be aware of the signs of food poisoning, such as nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

## Conclusion
Nutrition during the first trimester of pregnancy is crucial. Pregnant women should prioritize essential nutrients, such as folate and iron, and safe foods to support the development of the fetus. faqs.question: Why is folate important during the first trimester?
faqs.answer: Folate helps prevent birth defects of the brain and spine and supports the development of the fetus.

faqs.question: How can pregnant women ensure they are getting enough iron in their diet?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women can consume iron-rich foods, such as red meat, chicken, and fish, and should consult their doctor about iron supplements.

faqs.question: What foods should pregnant women avoid during the first trimester?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women should avoid foods like sushi, sashimi, and undercooked or raw meat, as they can contain bacteria and parasites that can harm the fetus.
